column3: NASB renders “an elder” as “an older man,” “rebuke” as “sharply rebuke,” and “exhort” as “appeal to.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “who are truly widows” as “who are widows indeed.”
NASB follows the critical text without “good and”; “to be devout” is rendered “to practice piety,” and “to give recompense” is “to make some return.”
NASB follows the critical text; “abandoned” is rendered “left alone,” and “supplications” is “entreaties.”
NASB renders “self-indulgence” as “wanton pleasure.”
NASB renders “command” as “Prescribe.”
NASB follows the critical text.
NASB renders “be enrolled” as “be put on the list.”
NASB renders “being borne witness to” as “having a reputation for,” “entertained strangers” as “shown hospitality to strangers,” and “imparted relief” as “assisted.”
NASB adds “to put … on the list” and renders “grow wanton against Christ” as “feel sensual desires in disregard of Christ.”
NASB renders “judgment” as “condemnation” and “first faith” as “previous pledge.”
NASB adds “to mention.”
NASB adds “widows” and renders “manage their households” as “keep house” and “the one opposing” as “the enemy.”
NASB adds “to follow.”
NASB follows the critical text (“woman who is a believer”) without “man or.”
NASB renders “straining in the word” as “work hard at preaching.”
NASB puts only the first quotation in capitals.
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text without “now”; it adds “of sinning.”
NASB follows the critical text without “Lord”; “earnestly testify” is rendered “solemnly charge,” and “prejudice” is “bias.”
NASB renders “soon” as “too hastily” and “pure” as “free from sin.”
NASB adds “exclusively.”
NASB renders “appear later” as “follow after.”
NASB follows the critical text; “works” is rendered “deeds.”
